title: [CQ-M03e] non-routine workload fixtures
description: Objective: Freeze five distinct non-routine workloads for the 20-case CQ-M03 matched corpus. Deliverable: packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.ts and non-routineWorkloads.test.ts, exporting this category's frozen dataset using the M03a workloadSnapshot contract. Frozen corpus contract (version 1): each workload has a unique category-prefixed id, category (maintenance/defect/refactor/non-routine), full startingCommit 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71, named repo source provenance, intendedBehavior/task instructions, deterministic snapshot digest over a documented sorted-path/UTF-8-byte encoding, initialFiles and separately held-out assessmentFiles (relative portable paths mapped to immutable UTF-8 strings), and explicit assessment rubric criteria/coverage tags. assessmentFiles contains executable independent black-box acceptance tests; it must not be copied into the coding snapshot. Include bounded reviewable Node ESM fixture source adaptations grounded in original Moe source, not twenty renamed toy cases, and label any reduced/adapted snapshot provenance honestly. No reference solution in coding inputs. Every case has a concrete original-state failure/required change and unchanged-acceptance positive and adversarial-negative controls; no agent judge/price/network dependency. The shared materializer owns only newly created os.tmpdir directories and offers fresh reset by new snapshot creation, never an arbitrary target root or Git reset/worktree operation. Category boundary: Five cases: add source-fingerprint invalidation to a small cached positive lookup; handle stale negative lookup when a new source export appears; add bounded multi-message pagination preserving unread remainder; allocate monotonic attempt generations from historical maximum despite deleted/gapped records; extend a small cross-role usage rollup that deduplicates durable provider identity and preserves unknown observations. Ground in util/cachedPlanPaths.ts, util/chatPayload.ts, state/attemptStore.ts and scripts/usage-report.mjs. Requirements specify new behavior and adversarial examples independently from any reference implementation; do not depend on forthcoming CQ context/runner APIs. Keep all fixture payloads/test-only corrected and plausible-wrong variants in these two files; no production edits, benchmark runs, aggregate corpus edits or edits to the dependency. Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts
definitionOfDone: Exactly five distinct non-routine fixtures validate against landed M03a contract, with frozen full starting commit, source provenance, intended behavior, content hashes and independent executable acceptance rubrics.

Each fixture has an unsolved original that fails at least one intended-change criterion, a test-only corrected variant passing the same unchanged rubric, and a plausible wrong variant rejected by it; no reference solution or assessment bytes enter coding inputs.

Cases retain category-specific invariants and explicit context/helper/caller/requirements/recipe coverage tags where applicable; snapshots and repeated resets are deterministic and never alter source checkout bytes.
Fresh cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits or Git-write commands; wrappers own landing. Preserve all peer/pre-existing dirty bytes.
Frozen benchmark/test scaffolding only; do not alter production behavior, enable verified-local, or claim VM/isolation certification.
Do not edit sibling category datasets/tests, the shared contract after it lands, or the M03 assembler; use explicit dependency updates for any contract change.

implementationPlan.description:
Prerequisites + harness (TDD red). Confirm CQ-M03a (task-44b44ccac62f4657890f98ff450738c8) is DONE/landed and READ the landed packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts; the planned names used here (validateWorkloads, digestFiles, digestWorkload, createCodingSnapshot, createAssessmentSnapshot, readSnapshotFiles, WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV, FROZEN_STARTING_COMMIT, SOURCE_REPOSITORY) may differ, so adapt and NEVER edit the contract (if it blocks a fixture, stop and use moe.report_blocked / an explicit dependency update). Read the grounding sources AT THE FROZEN COMMIT, read-only, via `git show 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71:<path>`: packages/moe-daemon/src/util/{cachedPlanPaths,chatPayload,chatBacklog}.ts, src/state/attemptStore.ts (decodeStoredGeneration/nextGeneration), scripts/usage-report.mjs (CQ-M02 changed it after the freeze, so use the 35cf53c bytes) and the 'Track negative searches too' paragraph of docs/plans/2026-10-24-ai-code-quality-and-context.md. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts (vitest, LF) importing `NON_ROUTINE_WORKLOADS` from './non-routineWorkloads.js' (red: not created yet) and the M03a API, following the shared corpus conventions:
(a) dataset tests: validateWorkloads(NON_ROUTINE_WORKLOADS) succeeds; exactly the five pinned ids in order ['non-routine-cached-lookup-fingerprint','non-routine-stale-negative-export-index','non-routine-chat-pagination-remainder','non-routine-monotonic-attempt-generation','non-routine-cross-role-usage-rollup']; every category 'non-routine'; frozen startingCommit; source.paths limited to the grounding paths; honest 'reduced'/'adapted' notes (they say which parts are synthetic); coverage tags include stale-negative-context on case 2 and unknown-preservation on case 5; per-case digestWorkload literals (pinned in step 3).
(b) one control harness: runAssessment(workload, candidateRoot) creates an assessment snapshot and runs `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--test', '--test-reporter=tap', ...each *.test.mjs], { cwd: assessmentRoot, env: { ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: '', [WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV]: candidateRoot }, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60000 })`, then parses `ok`/`not ok N - <criterion-id>: ...` TAP lines. Error handling: a spawn error, signal or timeout counts as a failure with a bounded excerpt, never as a pass.
(c) per-case controls (it.each over { id, corrected, wrong, wrongMustFail }), each variant in a FRESH coding snapshot: the original exits != 0 and fails at least one new-behavior criterion; the corrected variant exits 0 with EVERY criterion id ok; the plausible-wrong variant exits != 0 with wrongMustFail among its failures (not a crash).
(d) requirement independence: each workload's intendedBehavior states the new behavior and its adversarial examples in prose, and nothing in initialFiles hints at the corrected implementation.
(e) leakage: no initial file contains or equals any assessment or variant content, and no coding snapshot contains a *.test.mjs.
(f) determinism and reset: matching digests, and a mutation followed by a new snapshot restores snapshotDigest.
(g) source checkout untouched: sha256 of the dataset module and the grounding files is identical before and after the suite.
Dispose every handle; give the control tests a 120s timeout.

Cases 1-2: create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.ts exporting `NON_ROUTINE_WORKLOADS = validateWorkloads([...])` (workload objects only; variants live in the test file). Fixture code is bounded Node ESM .mjs adapted from the frozen source; every external effect (git, file reads, clock) is an INJECTED function, so no real git/network/CQ context or runner API is used. Assessments are self-contained node:test files that import the candidate via pathToFileURL(path.join(process.env[WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV], ...)), fail loudly when it is unset, and name tests `<criterion-id>: ...`.
CASE 1 'non-routine-cached-lookup-fingerprint' (tags cache-invalidation, source-fingerprint; source util/cachedPlanPaths.ts, reduced: cachedPlanRef plus rev-parse/ls-tree through an injected run(args)). initialFiles: src/cachedPlanPaths.mjs and src/pathLookupCache.mjs, whose createCachedPathLookup(run).lookup(branch, paths) memoizes FOUND paths by ref+path forever. intendedBehavior: every lookup resolves the ref to its commit once and serves a cached positive only when it was recorded at that same commit; otherwise re-query ls-tree. A resolution failure serves NO cached positives and caches nothing (fail closed). Misses are never cached. The cache is bounded to 256 entries, evicting the oldest. Criteria: serves-fresh-positive (same commit: ls-tree runs once across two lookups); invalidates-on-fingerprint-change (the ref advances to a commit without the path -> reported missing); fail-closed-on-resolution-error; no-negative-caching; bounded-cache. Corrected: commit-tagged entries. Plausible-wrong: correct invalidation, but on a rev-parse failure it falls back to cached positives -> wrongMustFail 'fail-closed-on-resolution-error'.
CASE 2 'non-routine-stale-negative-export-index' (tags stale-negative-context, cache-invalidation; source util/cachedPlanPaths.ts miss semantics + the docs/plans negative-search paragraph, adapted; the export index itself is synthetic, as the note says). initialFiles: src/helperFinder.mjs, whose createHelperFinder(readSource).find(name, modules) scans module text for an exported function/const/named-export of exactly `name` and caches every result - INCLUDING 'not found' - keyed by name only, plus two small sample modules. intendedBehavior: a cached negative is reused only for the same namespace (the sorted module list) AND the same per-module content fingerprints (sha256 of the text); a cached positive is re-verified against the current text of its module; a readSource failure yields { status: 'unknown' } and is never cached; matching is exact (boundedTailX does not match boundedTail). Criteria: detects-new-export (a module gains the export after a cached negative -> found), scope-aware-negative (a negative for [a,b] is not reused for [a,b,c]), detects-removed-export, read-errors-not-cached, exact-export-matching. Corrected: fingerprinted entries. Plausible-wrong: fingerprints content but caches a read failure as 'not found' -> wrongMustFail 'read-errors-not-cached'.
Pin snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest via digestFiles. Run only `npx vitest run src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts` in the isolated Linux copy; cases 1-2 controls green.

Cases 3-5 in the same two files, then freeze.
CASE 3 'non-routine-chat-pagination-remainder' (tags bounded-context, cursor-safety, pagination; source util/chatPayload.ts + util/chatBacklog.ts, adapted). initialFiles: src/chatPayload.mjs (CHAT_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_CHARS, chatMessageResponseCost, capChatMessagesToResponseBudget, truncateChatMessage(s) with a minimal truncateForBudget) and src/chatBacklog.mjs, whose readBacklog(messages, sinceId, maxContentChars) returns EVERY message after sinceId in one unbounded response. intendedBehavior: add readPage(messages, { sinceId, limit, maxContentChars, budget }) -> { messages, nextCursor, remaining }. A page respects both limit and the response budget (always at least one message); nextCursor is the id of the LAST DELIVERED message; remaining counts the unread messages after it; paging from nextCursor yields every message exactly once and in order, even when a single message is oversized; an unknown sinceId throws instead of silently restarting. Criteria: respects-limit-and-budget, cursor-is-last-delivered, pages-cover-all-exactly-once (loop until remaining 0, the concatenated ids equal the input ids), oversized-message-progress, rejects-unknown-cursor, truncation-flags-preserved. Corrected: limit, then budget cap, then cursor. Plausible-wrong: nextCursor = the last id of the limit window before the budget cap -> wrongMustFail 'pages-cover-all-exactly-once'.
CASE 4 'non-routine-monotonic-attempt-generation' (tags monotonic-identity, history-gaps; source state/attemptStore.ts, adapted: the fixture starts from the superseded count-based allocation, and the note says so). initialFiles: src/attemptGenerations.mjs, whose nextGeneration(store, taskId) returns the number of the task's records + 1. intendedBehavior: allocate max(store.highWater[taskId], the maximum stored generation of the task's records) + 1, persist the new high-water mark in store.highWater, never reuse a value after records are deleted or gapped, and keep tasks independent. A malformed stored generation (0, -1, 1.5, '3', NaN, above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) throws, naming the record, instead of being skipped. Exhaustion at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER throws with code 'ATTEMPT_GENERATION_EXHAUSTED'. Criteria: uses-historical-maximum ([1,2,5] -> 6), survives-deleted-highest (records [1,2] with highWater 5 -> 6), per-task-independence, rejects-malformed-stored, exhaustion-fails-closed, persists-high-water (repeated allocations strictly increase). Corrected: high-water plus max. Plausible-wrong: max over current records only -> wrongMustFail 'survives-deleted-highest'.
CASE 5 'non-routine-cross-role-usage-rollup' (tags usage-dedup, unknown-preservation, cross-role; source scripts/usage-report.mjs AT 35cf53c, reduced to the field list, the count/key helpers, identifiedGroups, mergeGroup and aggregate). initialFiles: scripts/usageRollup.mjs with those functions and per-provider/task aggregation only. intendedBehavior: add rollupByTask(rows) -> one entry per taskId across architect/worker/qa. It deduplicates by DURABLE provider identity (provider + session/event identity, exactly as identifiedGroups does) BEFORE summing, so a session reported by two roles or launches counts once. Rows without durable identity stay counted and visibly flagged (unidentifiedRecords), never dropped. Unknown counters stay unknown (excluded from observedTokens and counted in unknownRecords, never 0). Conflicting duplicates make that field unknown. The entry carries a per-role breakdown, and an overflow makes the total unknown. Criteria: dedupes-durable-identity, keeps-unidentified-visible, preserves-unknown-counters, conflicts-become-unknown, per-role-breakdown, overflow-unknown. Corrected: reuses identifiedGroups/mergeGroup, then groups by task. Plausible-wrong: deduplicates by launchId instead of provider session/event identity -> wrongMustFail 'dedupes-durable-identity'.
Freeze: pin snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest per workload and the five digestWorkload literals. Make the whole file green with focused runs in the isolated Linux copy.

The one verification gate. Build a FRESH synchronized isolated copy (recipe in planningNotes; it must include the landed M03a contract), add the two owned files' working-tree bytes, and with Linux-only PATH run exactly: `cd <copy>/packages/moe-daemon && PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin npx vitest run src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts` (fresh exit 0; report actual pass/skip counts). Then run `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` with the same PATH (the dataset compiles into dist; vitest does not typecheck). Repeat the focused run once to show repeatability and confirm no `moe-workload-*` temp dirs remain. Never touch the original Windows node_modules or any package-lock.json, and confirm the tested files are byte-identical (sha256) to the working tree. Keep the command and output tail for complete_task.

Exactly one adversarial self-review of the two-file diff (load adversarial-self-review). Challenge each case. Is the new behavior specified independently of any reference implementation, with adversarial examples, in intendedBehavior? Does the original fail a new-behavior criterion for the right reason? Does the corrected variant pass every criterion, and the wrong variant fail the named one rather than crash? Are the subtle invariants actually exercised - fail-closed resolution (1), read errors never cached plus exact matching (2), the cursor is the last DELIVERED message with exactly-once coverage (3), the high-water mark survives deletion and malformed values throw (4), dedupe by durable identity with unknowns kept visible (5)? Are all external effects injected, with no real git, fs-outside-snapshot, clock or network dependence? Are provenance notes honest (synthetic index in case 2, the superseded count allocation in case 4, the reduced usage-report from 35cf53c in case 5)? Are template-literal escapes and digests stable? Confirm: no production/daemon edit, no edit to workloadSnapshot.ts or sibling datasets, no dependence on forthcoming CQ context/runner APIs, no Git or .moe writes, no benchmark/VM/readiness claims, and no substring from the project's global forbiddenPatterns (project.globalRails) in either file, fixture strings included. Fix findings with tests; if any byte changed after step 4, rerun the step-4 commands fresh and use that output for complete_task.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- **Frozen sources (read via `git show 35cf53c:<path>`):**
  - **cachedPlanPaths.ts:** literal-only refs/remotes/origin/<branch>; rev-parse --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}; ls-tree --literal-pathspecs; every refusal is a named miss.
  - **chatPayload.ts:** CHAT_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_CHARS = 220; capChatMessagesToResponseBudget keeps a prefix, delivers at least one, and returns the dropped tail. chatBacklog.ts caps, then truncates.
  - **attemptStore.ts:** decodeStoredGeneration throws on a non-positive-safe-integer; nextGeneration = max over records + 1, throws ATTEMPT_GENERATION_EXHAUSTED at MAX_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, and is never a count.
  - **usage-report.mjs:** identifiedGroups merges by key(provider,'session',sessionId) for measured session scope and key(provider, scope, event|missing-event, eventId). mergeGroup makes conflicting fields null and counts conflicts. aggregate gives observedTokens/unknownRecords/overflowFields.
- **Files moved after the freeze.** CQ-M02 (db3172e) changed usage-report.mjs and CQ-M01b changed the delivery files, so always ground in 35cf53c.
- **Filename:** the dataset filename contains a hyphen (non-routineWorkloads.ts); import it as './non-routineWorkloads.js'. The id prefix is 'non-routine-', matching the category.
- **Isolated Linux copy recipe:**
  1. `D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-m03e-test.XXXXXX)`
  2. `git -C /mnt/d/projexts/moes archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon docs scripts CLAUDE.md .gitignore package.json | tar -x -C "$D"`
  3. Copy the owned files' working-tree bytes into the copy.
  4. `ln -s "$(cat /tmp/moe-linux-test-root.latest)/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules" "$D/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules"`
  5. Run with PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin.
  Re-copy before each focused run.
planningNotes.risks:
- **Vacuous controls:** a crash or syntax error must never count as a correct rejection. The wrong variant must fail the NAMED criterion, and the corrected variant must report every criterion id as ok.
- **Case 2:** use a real sha256 (node:crypto) for fingerprints, and an exact-name export regex with word boundaries. A commented-out export may be treated either way as long as intendedBehavior states which.
- **Case 3:** the exactly-once loop must terminate (bound its iterations) even for a broken candidate.
- **Case 4:** use plain in-memory store objects passed by the assessment. Never touch .moe/attempts.
- **Case 5:** use receipt rows as plain objects. Never read logs/moe-usage from disk.
- **Template-literal escaping and forbidden patterns:** escape backslashes, backticks and `${` in fixture code. The project's global forbiddenPatterns are raw substring checks that also apply to fixture strings and longer identifiers.
- **Dependency:** M03a is unlanded at planning time. Wait for DONE and adapt to its real exports without editing it.
- **Repo hygiene:** no production edits, no Git/.moe writes, and preserve the shared tree's peer/pre-existing dirty bytes. Focused runs only; one final gate.
